questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Which university subjects lead to the best-paid jobs
How to pay for a university degree without getting into debt
Taking a year off before university, and why it matters now
The best countries to travel to after finishing school
questions.why: Neil says they're talking about taking a gap year and why it has become more important.

questions.q: Did Georgina take a gap year?
options: Yes, she did
No, she went straight to university
No, she didn't go to university
She started one but didn't finish it
questions.why: When Neil asks if she took a year off, she says, 'I did.'

questions.q: Why did Meg take a gap year?
options: She wasn't sure she wanted to go to university at all
Her parents told her she should travel around Asia first
She failed her exams and needed time to take them again
She wanted to apply with real results, not predicted ones
questions.why: She wanted to wait for her official results rather than use predicted grades.

questions.q: What did Meg want her gap year to be like?
options: Relaxing, with no work at all
Both useful and fun
Spent entirely studying
As cheap as possible
questions.why: She wanted to do 'something productive and something that would just be good fun'.

questions.q: How did Tom feel about gap years?
options: He hadn't really heard of them, and they cost too much
He deeply regretted not taking one after leaving school
He thought they were a waste of time and of good money
His parents offered to pay for one, but he refused
questions.why: He calls it 'an alien concept' and says it would have been far too expensive.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention Chris Rea after Tom's comments?
options: To agree that gap years are too expensive
To give advice about choosing a university
To show a gap year doesn't have to cost a lot
To explain how to get better exam results
questions.why: Neil says Tom thought it'd be too expensive, but according to Chris Rea it needn't cost a lot.

questions.q: According to Chris Rea, how have gap years changed?
options: They are now mostly spent travelling around the world
They are now much shorter, often only a few months long
Fewer students take them now because of the high cost
They have become more practical and focused on skills
questions.why: He says the gap year has become 'much more practical', with a focus on employability skills.

questions.q: What does Chris Rea say about employers?
options: They only care about degree results
They value any experience and skills you gained
They prefer students who didn't take a gap year
They want to see travel experience
questions.why: He says from an employer's point of view, any experience and skills acquisition is valuable.
